chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the fasting person who kisses the slave girl and the wife?' He said: 'As for the old man like me and like you, there is no problem. And as for the young, lustful man, no, because he is not safe from desire, and kissing is one of the two lustful desires.' I said, 'So what do you think regarding someone like me who has a slave girl, and he plays with her?' He said to me, 'You are lustful, O Abu Hazim. How is your food intake?' I said, 'If I am satiated, it harms me, and if I am hungry, it weakens me.' He said: 'I am like that. So, how are you with women?' I said, 'And there is nothing [to it].' He said: 'But I, O Abu Hazim, whatever I desire to do, that happens from me, until I do it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on kissing while fasting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the older, experienced man and the young, impulsive man regarding the permissibility of kissing and foreplaying while fasting, emphasizing that the primary concern is the risk of progressing to sexual intercourse. The Imam employs a metaphor of hunger and satiety to illustrate how excessive intimacy can weaken the spiritual focus of the fast, yet he acknowledges his own susceptibility to desire despite his knowledge. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that acts permissible in themselves may become discouraged or prohibited based on the individual's capacity to avoid the next stage of desire (al-wasf al-shahwi).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Dawood Bin Al No’man, from Mansour Bin Hazim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the Fasting one who kisses the slave girl and the wife?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the old man like me<sup>asws</sup> and like you, so there is no problem, and as for the young man, so no, because he would not be safe, and the kissing is one of the two lustful desires’. I said, ‘So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding the likes of me who happens to have the slave girl for him, so he plays with her?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Do you need it, O Abu Hazim? How is your food intake?’ I said, ‘If I am satiated, it harms me, and if I am hungry, it weakens me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am like that. So, how are you and the women?’ I said, ‘And there is nothing’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But I<sup>asws</sup>, O Abu Hazim, whatever I<sup>asws</sup> so desire to, that happens from me<sup>asws</sup>, until I<sup>asws</sup> do it’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dawud ibn al-Nu’man from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who kisses a slave-girl or the woman. He (the Imam) said, ‘For an old man like you and I, it is not harmful but for a lustful young man it is negative and not safe; kissing is one of the two lustful activities (sexual intercourse and kissing).’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘What do you say about a person like me who plays with his slave-girl?’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Are you lustful, O abu Hazim, how is your desire for food?’ I replied, ‘If I am full it is harmful and if I am hungry then it makes me weak.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘So am I.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘How are you and women?’ I said, ‘There is nothing.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘O abu Hazim, if I desire something to happen from me I make it happen.’”
